channel.description: Latest articles from Providence Magazine – Bias and Credibility (providencemag.com)

item.title: The Case Against Christian Nationalism - Providence
item.description: Christian Nationalism has many definitions, which makes the term unhelpful

item.title: Reinhold Niebuhr and Geoeconomic Competition - Providence
item.description: What does Christian realism have to say about competition with China for economically critical rare earth minerals?

item.title: Trump’s Objectives in Iran and the Fog of War - Providence
item.description: Despite the level of uncertainty swirling around Iran and how the U.S. can be expected to proceed, the truth is that stopping Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons has been a long-stated objective of the Trump administration

item.title: Trump’s Next Moves to Reassert Western Hemisphere Primacy - Providence
item.description: The recent gathering of Western Hemisphere leaders in Doral, Florida, signaled the emergence of an American-led strategy focused on countering fentanyl, stopping illegal Chinese fishing fleets, and investing in Latin America’s emerging 5G networks

item.title: A New World Order… of Baseball? - Providence
item.description: Though the Olympics and FIFA World Cup dominate international sports diplomacy, the World Baseball Classic showcases the soft power of America’s pastime across a surprisingly aligned set of nations.

item.title: Caught in the Crossfire: The Growing Vulnerability of Middle Eastern Religious Minorities - Providence
item.description: The killing of a Maronite priest in southern Lebanon highlights a broader reality: across the Middle East, religious minorities are increasingly caught between state collapse, militant power, and regional conflict—with grave consequences for both their survival and U.S. interests.

item.title: How American Politics Became Footnotes to Catholicism - Providence
item.description: How Catholicism, the religion of outsiders and immigrants, became the shared political grammar of both the American left and right

item.title: War Powers, Congress, and the Executive: From the American Revolution to War with Iran - Providence
item.description: While President Trump’s decision to attack Iran has prompted renewed debates over executive war-making power, arguments about the proper roles of the executive and legislature in military action date back to America’s founding

item.title: Review of “If Russia Wins: A Scenario” - Providence
item.description: A new book explores the distressingly plausible scenario of Ukraine being forced into an unfavorable truce with Russia—a possibility that should unsettle so-called “realists” skeptical of supporting Ukraine.

item.title: Americans have Become Desensitized to the Bloody Reality of War - Providence
item.description: Through a combination of technological precision, geographic removal, and a limited segment of the population engaged in military service, most Americans have become highly insulated from the tragic realities of war
